CHAP. XXIX. 
 
  Job, after pausing a little while, shews, what comfort he formerly had   in his house and family, ver. 1-6.   What honour and power he had in his country, ver. 7-10.   What good he did as a magistrate, ver. 11-17.   And what a prospect he had of the continuance of his prosperity,   ver. 18-25
V. 2. Preserved-From all those miseries which now I feel.
V. 3. Darkness-I passed safely through many difficulties, and dangers, and common calamities.

V. 7. Seat-When I caused the seat of justice to be set for me. By this, and several other expressions, it appears that Job was a magistrate.  Street-In that open place, near the gate, where the people assembled for the administration of justice.
V. 10. Cleaved-It lay as still as if he had done so.
V. 11. Witness-Gave testimony to my pious, and just, and blameless conversation.
V. 14. Put on, &c.-Perhaps he did not wear these: but his steady justice was to him instead of all those ornaments.
V. 18. Multiply-See how apt even good men are, to set death at a distance from them!
V. 20. Glory-My reputation was growing every day.  Bow-My strength which is signified by a bow,
, because in ancient times the bow and arrows were the principal instruments of war.
V. 22. Dropped-As the rain, which when it comes down gently upon the earth, is most acceptable and beneficial to it.

V. 24. Laughed-Carried myself so familiarly with them, that they could scarce believe their eyes and ears.  Cast not down-They were cautious not to give me any occasion to change my countenance towards them.

V. 25. I chose-They sought to me for advice in all difficult cases, and I directed them what methods they  should take.  Sat-As a prince or judge, while they stood waiting for my counsel.  A king-Whose presence puts life, and courage, into the whole army.  As one-As I was ready to comfort any afflicted persons, so my consolations were always welcome to them.
